holidays.name: National Martini Day
holidays.description: Shaken or stirred, olive or twist, today is the day to raise a chilled, long-stemmed glass to the cocktail that has come to stand for sophistication. Bars across the country celebrate with classic recipes and creative riffs.
holidays.origin: National Martini Day is an unofficial observance, and nobody is sure who started it. It has been marked on June 19 since at least the late 1990s. The drink's own history is just as hazy. Some credit a 19th-century cocktail called the Martinez, which was first printed in a San Francisco bartending guide in 1887. Others point to the Gold Rush town of Martinez, California, or to an early 1900s New York bartender named Martini.
holidays.funFact: The martini's origin story has at least three competing versions, and no one has settled the debate. Fans of Humphrey Bogart, Ernest Hemingway and James Bond all claim the drink as part of the family tree.

holidays.name: Garfield the Cat Day
holidays.description: This is a day for lasagna, Monday-hating and napping. Fans honor the sarcastic orange tabby who is famous for loving food and avoiding exercise.
holidays.origin: The date marks June 19, 1978. On that day Jim Davis's comic strip Garfield went into national syndication. It had run locally since 1976 under the title Jon, which was named for the cat's owner. The cat soon became the star, and the strip grew into a worldwide phenomenon.
holidays.funFact: The strip started out centered on Jon Arbuckle, the cat's owner. Garfield took over as the main attraction, and the strip became one of the most widely syndicated comics in the world.

holidays.name: International Box Day
holidays.description: This day celebrates the simple joy of the cardboard box, and cats are its unofficial mascots. Cat owners are encouraged to leave out empty boxes so their pets can climb in, squeeze in and stare up at you with satisfaction.
holidays.origin: International Box Day is an unofficial observance. It was created to encourage cat owners to set out empty cardboard boxes for their cats to enjoy.
holidays.funFact: Cats are famously drawn to boxes, even ones that look too small for them. Enclosed spaces can help cats feel secure and less stressed, so a plain cardboard box doubles as a cozy hideout.
